INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE-CLOSURE REVIEW a3 — CONSTRUCTION-S4-VALIDATE-R01v2 (ADR 0186)
Same independent reviewer. Bounded, evidence-only follow-up to the a2 APPROVE. I do not reopen the a2 source verdict; production and functional-test sources are unchanged (construction.gd ec758c4f, save_owner_construction.gd f275eede, all test files at their a2 hashes, confirmed against release-checks-a2/source-manifest.json). I executed nothing; every result is as supplied.

=== VERDICT ===
ALL REMAINING AUDITABILITY CONDITIONS CLOSE. N1, N2, N3, N4, N5 and N7 are closed; L4 (CI pin) now closes on supplied evidence rather than on assertion. The one executable change (argparse --output-dir) is correct, fail-closed and semantically inert. Source approval from a2 stands unchanged. Named residuals below are carried, not closed — none is new risk and none blocks. Exact committed identity and both CI checks remain parent gates and are not claimed here. I make no claim that any of the five unwitnessed bridge array anchors was tested.

=== CONDITION CLOSURE ===

N1 (durable evidence) — CLOSED. metadata-final-a3/result.json is a full 62-entry per-case record: 60 fault units plus baseline-before/after, every entry valid_execution true, pure_checks 5, pure_mismatches 0, forward_exact true, early_priority true, passed true, seconds recorded. It pins source_sha256 at the candidate hashes (construction.gd ec758c4f, save_owner_construction.gd f275eede, plus catalog.gd, building_definitions.gd, save_component_columns_schema.gd) and the observer hash, and its proposal_rebase now records proposed-vs-executed for BOTH construction.gd and save_owner_construction.gd — stricter than the a2 record, which named only the owner. The five witnesses that close F2/F3 are present with their exact per-case detail rather than an aggregate: the four dictionary-key faults (build-materials-, furniture-materials-, upgrade-materials-, upgrade-work-mwu-actual-key-stringname) each reach COLUMN_SOURCE_METADATA through the pure preflight, and coherent-building-bill-pair-count records pure_source_code "" with bridge detail "Construction owner1 metadata: building bill pair counts entry 0 does not match the frozen source" at first_gate "4/independent array anchor" — i.e. the record itself shows the pure path ACCEPTING while the bridge anchor refuses, which is the property that makes it a bridge-independence witness. The a2 gap (detail destroyed with the temp dir) is gone.

N2 (source traceability of the focus run) — CLOSED. release-checks-a2/focus.json now carries a source_sha256 block naming six files, and I verified every one against the supplied pre-run source-manifest.json: construction.gd ec758c4f, save_owner_construction.gd f275eede, test_construction_columns.gd ab28c4f1, test_save_owner_construction.gd d42cc22c, test_construction_retired_histories.gd 8b2bbbfd, construction_columns_focus.gd fd24cddd. All six match exactly. The identity_provenance field states the correct derivation — taken from the immutable pre-run manifest and bracketed by release-checks-a2/result.json's post-run source_unchanged:true across all five steps — and explicitly disclaims using the deterministic log digest as identity. That is the right construction: the 96/2354 focus run is now provably tied to the candidate source by a pre-run manifest plus a post-run unchanged assertion, not by an artifact that is byte-identical between revisions.

N3 (unchanged-code proof scope) — CLOSED. row-semantic-unchanged-code-proof.json now enumerates 17 functions, adding exactly the three I identified as missing: _ref_gate_refusal, _declared_bill_pairs_for_row and _column_flag_scan_refusal. Those three are the ones several row/flag mutants target (the four reference faults, allow-empty-bill-awaiting, and the three flag-two-permitted cases plus flags-after-row-semantics), so the proof now covers the functions its own transfer argument depends on. I confirmed all three unchanged by reading in a2; the artifact now says so.

N4 (pre-/post-rebase labelling) — CLOSED as labelling. post-review-source-and-target-verification.json now carries a top-level original_vs_rebased statement saying plans[] measures the ORIGINAL proposal strings and that row_semantic_rebase plus row-allocation-fault-proposal-rebased.json supersede the five 0-occurrence WORKERS entries. A later reader can no longer take all_exact_once:false as a failure. RESIDUAL: row-allocation-fault-proposal-rebased.json is referenced but not supplied in this packet, so the claim that all 39 final targets match exactly once with unchanged executable old/new bodies is labelled-and-asserted, not inspectable here.

N5 (index staleness) — CLOSED as labelling. candidate-validation-index.json adds campaigns_status stating the historical campaigns are retained unchanged and superseded for final-source runtime status by final_source_evidence, and that their old pending notes are historical rather than open gates. final_source_evidence now also links full (5108/528323, source unchanged) and static (17 checks), and points metadata at metadata-final-a3 with its retained logs and harness. remaining is reduced to this evidence follow-up plus exact commit and both CI checks. Minor: the literal "Final current-source portable allocation rerun pending" note still sits inside campaigns[allocation-a1] and is neutralised only by the blanket campaigns_status line — correct under the retain-history-unchanged policy, but it requires reading campaigns_status first.

N7 (contract text) — CLOSED, and broader than asked. The contract gains two sections. "Independent review key/anchor closure" records the four extra bill/work dictionaries requiring TYPE_STRING stored keys, keeps bill element checks separate, and requires explicit ordered bridge anchor comparisons rather than a dynamic check table with identical labels/order/refusals. "Final independent review clarifications" then names all eight dictionaries explicitly, and — beyond N7 — writes L1, L2 and L7 into the contract: the direct-source-vs-bridge bill-quantity asymmetry, the obligation on future persistence coordinators to handle raw COLUMN_* refusal codes, and the state_bytes diagnostic's same-type/same-length transposition limit with the explicit statement that it defines no save format and establishes no capture/apply correctness. In a2 I could not verify these because the contract was not supplied; they are now recorded in the owning document rather than carried only by review prose.

L4 (CI pin) — CLOSED on evidence. .github/workflows/tests.yml pins GODOT_VERSION 4.7.2, downloads that exact tagged release, puts it on PATH via GITHUB_PATH and prints godot --version. Both Construction gates are present and invoked: "Construction source and schema fault injection" (tools/test_construction_metadata_preflights.py) and "Construction borrowed-buffer allocation discriminator" (tools/test_construction_allocation.py), alongside ./tools/run_tests.sh for the full suite. This was accepted-on-assertion in a2 and is now verifiable.

=== THE ONE EXECUTABLE CHANGE (argparse) ===
tools/test_construction_metadata_preflights.py a44d5a13 differs from the a2 revision only by: `import argparse`; four argparse lines (parser construction, --output-dir, parse_args, conditional mkdir); and the `out=` selection. I read the rest against the a2 version and it is unchanged — the -O guard, the core-path fault guard, the 55+5 plan-length and 60-unique-id assertions, the per-edit exactly-once assertion, the per-case loop and expectations, and the final `len(results)==62 and all passed` assertion.
Correctness and safety of the new option:
- `if not __debug__: raise SystemExit(...)` remains the FIRST statement in main(), so it still precedes argparse, the output-directory creation and any engine launch. -O cannot strip it and cannot reach a write.
- `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)` refuses an existing directory, so a rerun cannot silently clobber a retained evidence record; failure raises before any clone or engine run (fail-closed).
- --output-dir is operator-supplied and writes only logs, result.json and the copied executed-harness.py. It does not widen the fault-injection surface, which remains governed by the unchanged godot/scripts/core/*.gd path guard. No new security exposure.
- `shutil.copy2(__file__, out/'executed-harness.py')` now lands durably, so the retained record is accompanied by the exact harness that produced it.
- Cosmetic only: the TemporaryDirectory context is still entered when --output-dir is supplied, leaving one unused temp dir for the run's duration. No leak (context-managed), no behavioural effect.
Default behaviour (CI) is unchanged: no --output-dir, temp output, aggregate line only.

=== SUPPLIED COMPLETION RESULTS (recorded, not executed by me) ===
- release-checks-a2/result.json: five steps (import, focus, metadata, allocation, full) all exit 0 and passed, with source_unchanged:true across the whole sequence. Full suite 5108 tests / 528323 assertions / 0 failures, expected_counts matched, leak_diagnostic_lines empty. The nine ERROR lines are all SettlementSystem stock-integrity and ui_frame_builder negative-path diagnostics, unrelated to Construction, and are accepted by the harness's own error_multiset_matches_expected comparison; I cannot independently baseline that expected multiset from this packet.
- static-a3.json: 17 checks, all exit 0, same set as static-a2. Worth noting one substantive confirmation: validate_save_registry_handoff --source-root . still reports 554 persisted packed fields and 603 canonical records, identical to a2 — so the append-only Columns/SOURCE_*/COLUMN_* region introduced no new packed column and no undeclared persistent state. generate_component_columns_schema --check and test_component_columns_schema also still pass, so the section-4 metadata is unmoved.

=== RESIDUALS CARRIED (unchanged in substance, all previously stated) ===
R1. Five of ten bridge array anchors remain without an executed discrimination witness — building keys, furniture keys, furniture bill pair counts, upgrade ids, upgrade bill pair counts. I verified all ten calls and all ten source pairings by reading in a2. The a3 note correctly declines to invent an upgrade-ID witness that the earlier independent tier-two-key anchor would mask. No coverage is claimed for any of the five.
R2. The 39 row-semantic and 6 negative-phase mutation campaigns remain executed only at the pre-repair owner hash, transferred by an unchanged-executable-text argument that is now fully scoped (17 functions) and explicitly labelled as code identity rather than a new runtime claim. The positive direction of those same rules is re-executed at the candidate hash by the 96/2354 focus.
R3. N6: _array_anchor's untyped Array parameters mean a future mis-pairing would surface at runtime rather than statically. Latent; all ten current pairings verified.
R4. F4: the TYPE-before-WORKERS index precondition is carried by call order plus a docstring, in a codebase where tests do call private statics. Latent; no caller violates it today.
R5. New, minor: row-allocation-fault-proposal-rebased.json is referenced but not supplied here (see N4).
R6. New, minor: CI runs the metadata fault campaign, the allocation discriminator and the full suite, but not the focused runner or the projection-purity / row-semantic / negative-phase mutation campaigns. Those remain manual, so their currency depends on the evidence records rather than on a gate — worth a future CI step for the focus runner at least, since it is the only current-hash execution of the twelve real retirement histories and the 82944-row image.
R7. New, trivial: the -O refusal evidence was produced against the pre-argparse harness revision. The guard is unchanged and is the first statement of main(), which I verified by reading, so the property holds at a44d5a13; it was simply not re-executed.
R8. Scope limits from a1/a2 are unchanged and not restated: no whole-file save identity, no CRC/digest, no section-5 ledger, no capture/apply, no cross-owner or same-file binding, no disk transaction or rollback, no live restoration, no process-RSS or native-overhead qualification, no timing claim, no big-endian evidence, no exhaustive-mutation claim.

=== CONCLUSION ===
The auditability conditions are closed. The a2 source approval stands unchanged and is not reopened. Nothing here authorizes source application, merge or milestone acceptance; exact committed identity and both CI checks remain parent gates.
